definition: A specialization of MLOps focused specifically on the operational challenges of deploying and maintaining large language model applications, such as prompt versioning, evaluation, and cost monitoring.
details: LLMOps addresses concerns distinct from traditional MLOps, including prompt engineering workflows, retrieval pipeline management, token-cost tracking, and evaluation of open-ended generative outputs.

explainer.lead: LLMOps is the operations discipline for LLM applications, covering prompt versioning, evaluation and cost monitoring. It matters because generative systems change behaviour with every prompt or model swap, so ordinary deployment practices are not enough.

tiers.eli5: It is the maintenance garage for AI apps: keeping track of which instructions were used, checking the car still runs, and watching the fuel bill.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers version prompts like code, run evaluations before promoting changes, and track token cost per feature; a frequent pitfall is shipping a prompt edit without a regression eval, silently degrading quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined by contrast with MLOps: instead of retraining weights, the managed artefacts are prompts, retrieval indexes and model versions, evaluated on open-ended outputs; limits include noisy automatic metrics and non-reproducible model APIs.

explainer.example: A team keeps prompt v12 in version control, gates its release on an eval suite, and rolls back to v11 after scores drop on summarisation.
